dedupe_keys.name: neighborhood atlas area deprivation index adi united states census block groups

description: The Neighborhood Atlas shares the Area Deprivation Index (ADI), which ranks every United States census block group by neighbourhood disadvantage using income, education, employment and housing quality measures from the American Community Survey five-year data. It is maintained by the University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health. Rankings are given nationally as percentiles and within each state as deciles, and the latest maps use the 2024 ADI. The website offers interactive maps for a state or the whole country and a download tool for rankings by region. The ADI is free and available to the public, but downloading needs a free user account and agreement to the site's terms of use, and users are asked to cite the 2018 New England Journal of Medicine article. Caveats: the ADI inherits the errors of American Community Survey estimates, and the maintainers state that values should be used only at block group level because linking them to ZIP codes, tracts or other units is not validated. Simulation uses: adding a social vulnerability layer to hazard exposure and service disruption analyses, weighting equity in facility location and recovery prioritisation, and stratifying emergency service outcomes. Related records: the HRSA shortage areas (data-hrsa-shortage-areas-hpsa-mua) and County Health Rankings (data-county-health-rankings-analytic-data) cover health access and outcomes.
